title: Merge Triplets to Form Target Triplet
prompt:
You are given `triplets` and a `target` triplet. In one operation you may pick two triplets `i` and `j` and set `triplets[j]` to their element-wise max `[max(a_i,a_j), max(b_i,b_j), max(c_i,c_j)]`. Return whether `target` can appear as an element of `triplets` after any number of operations.

**Example**: `triplets = [[2,5,3],[1,8,4],[1,7,5]]`, `target = [2,7,5]` → `true` (merge the first and third).

**Constraints**: `1 ≤ triplets.length ≤ 10^5`, values `1 ≤ x ≤ 1000`.

tests.note: no triplet reaches 3 in the first slot

hints: A merge takes a max, so values only go up. What does that mean for a triplet with any value above the target?
Such a triplet can never be used. Merging all the other ("safe") triplets never overshoots the target in any position.
Among safe triplets, record for each position k whether some `t[k] == target[k]`. The answer is true only if all three positions are hit.

solution.explanation: Values never decrease under max, so a triplet that exceeds the target anywhere is unusable. Merging every safe triplet gives the largest reachable result that stays ≤ target in each position. That equals the target exactly when each coordinate is matched by some safe triplet. O(n) time, O(1) space.
